name: SGH Warsaw School of Economics
summary: Public economics university in Warsaw, founded in 1906, about 10,000 students; four English bachelor's in business, economics and data.

ib.text: Any IB Diploma qualifies and proves B2 English; no subject minimums. Non-Polish applicants must pass SGH's short online entrance test (30% pass mark), which adds no points.

programmes.name: Global Business, Finance and Governance
programmes.about: Economics, finance, management, marketing and international trade for work in international business and finance, with a minor in EU integration, global development and governance, international business or international finance; four double-degree options.
programmes.overview: The course blends economics, finance, management, international business, marketing and international trade with training in data collection and analysis, and teaching includes projects and research tasks. You choose one of four tracks: European Economic Integration Towards Global Challenges (EU institutions and policy), Global Development and Governance (sustainable development and international organisations), International Business, or International Finance (capital markets, exchange rates, financial risk). Double degrees are possible with partners in China, Germany and South Korea. Graduates start in finance, sales, logistics and marketing roles in companies, NGOs, government agencies and international organisations, or continue to a master's or doctorate at SGH.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents checked, then pass the online test; if oversubscribed, places go by when you confirm your offer letter. 80 of 170 places for non-Poles (2026/27).

programmes.name: International Economics
programmes.about: How trade, international finance and European integration shape firms and states: three semesters of economics, accounting and statistics, then international economics, business, and politics and law, with a minor in the digital economy, EU membership or international entrepreneurship.
programmes.overview: The first three semesters cover micro- and macroeconomics, management and accounting, finance, economic and social policy, European integration, statistics and two foreign languages. The last three follow an economics, business or politics and law track, with courses such as international competitiveness, international finance, corporate finance, international marketing, international organisations and public international law. You can add a minor in Digital World Economy, Economics of EU membership or International Entrepreneurship, and double degrees are offered with Peking University, Pforzheim, Kyungpook National University and Kyiv National Economic University. Graduates go into international companies, EU administration, international organisations such as the OECD, IMF and UN, research institutes, media or their own business.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents checked, then pass the online test; if oversubscribed, places go by when you confirm your offer letter. 35 of 60 places for non-Poles (2026/27).

programmes.name: Management
programmes.about: How organisations work and how to plan, organise, motivate and control them, grounded in economics, with a minor in entrepreneurship, marketing or project management; aimed at specialist and junior manager roles or running your own business.
programmes.overview: The course teaches how organisations operate, with management sciences and economics, the basic functions of planning, organising, motivating, monitoring and coordinating, and the formulation, planning and control of projects. Learning is practical, through project work, the student internship programme and exchange options. You specialise in Entrepreneurship, Marketing or Project Management, and double degrees are available with Peking University (Guanghua School of Management) and European University Viadrina. Graduates become specialists or middle managers in businesses, non-profits and public administration, start their own firms, or move on to a master's degree.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents checked, then pass the online test; if oversubscribed, places go by when you confirm your offer letter. 55 of 90 places for non-Poles (2026/27).

programmes.name: Quantitative Methods in Economics and Information Systems
programmes.about: Economics and finance with statistics, econometrics, operations research, programming and information-systems design, taught in small lab groups, with a minor in econometrics or decision analysis. It assumes school maths and probability; no coding needed.
programmes.overview: You study mathematical analysis and linear algebra, probability and mathematical statistics, research design, demography, mathematical economics, econometrics, operational research, finance and insurance mathematics, programming, information systems design and databases. Laboratory classes in small groups put modern tools to use on real examples and empirical analysis. You choose between two specialisations: Econometrics, for building and interpreting models in economics, finance and social sciences, or Methods of Decision Analysis, with risk assessment and data analysis. Graduates work in organisations that apply mathematical, statistical, econometric and information tools, start their own business, or go on to a master's degree; exchange, double degree and Erasmus+ options exist.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents checked, then pass the online test; if oversubscribed, places go by when you confirm your offer letter. 40 of 70 places for non-Poles (2026/27).

notes: The English degrees cost the same €2,500 a semester for everyone, Polish citizens included; EU citizenship makes only SGH's Polish-taught study free.
Places are not ranked on grades: when a programme is full, SGH goes by the time you confirm your offer letter, so register, upload and sit the test early.
An IB Diploma needs no NAWA recognition statement; admitted students hand in the originals in person in Warsaw, usually in late September.
